rationale: 614.12 states that to determine which replacement effects modify how a permanent enters, the game checks continuous effects that already exist and would apply to it; Dearly Departed's graveyard-based effect exists at that check because the cards haven't changed zones yet.
104.4a states that if all players remaining in a game lose simultaneously the game is a draw, which is exactly why neither player won the subgame and both count as players who didn't win it.
707.10c states that once the copy's controller decides the copy's targets, the copy is put onto the stack with those targets, so the copy never targets Whiskervale Forerunner at any point.
204.2 states an object with a color indicator is each color denoted by that indicator, which is why Dryad Arbor is green rather than colorless.
104.5 states a player who loses the game leaves it, and 729.2 states the subgame is set up by each player (i.e., the players still in the game) following rule 103, so Clay is not part of it.
104.5 states Charli left the game on losing, leaving two players; 103.8a states that in a two-player game the player who plays first skips their first draw step.

101.4 states simultaneous choices are made by the active player first, then nonactive players in turn order (with the 'each player sacrifices a creature' example), and 101.4b states a player knows the choices made by previous players.

608.2d states a player can't choose an illegal or impossible option while applying an effect, and 701.21a states you can only sacrifice a permanent you control; Slum Reaper itself is Ashlyn's only creature.
109.5 states 'you' on an object refers to that object's controller or would-be controller, so on the granted ability now on Douser of Lights it means the permanent's current controller, Nico.
102.4 states that in a game that isn't a multiplayer game between teams, 'your team' means the same thing as 'you'.
103.1 states the players determine which one of them chooses who takes the first turn, so the die-roll winner may choose the opponent as the starting player.

103.5b states an action allowed 'any time you could mulligan' is taken at the time that player would declare a mulligan, and 103.5 states the starting player declares first, then each other player in turn order.
103.6 states that after mulligans the starting player takes any opening-hand actions, then each other player in turn order does the same; the sequence passes once, so Ari gets no second chance.

727.1a states the player who controlled the restarting ability is the starting player, so Ameer can't use Gemstone Caverns; 727.4 states the restart effect finishes resolving just before the first untap step, i.e. after opening-hand actions.

103.6/103.6a state opening-hand actions (putting Leyline onto the battlefield) happen right after mulligans, while 727.4 states Karn's exiled cards arrive only as the restart effect finishes resolving just before the first untap step.

303.4j states an Aura doesn't move if the effect would attach it to something it can't legally enchant (it's no longer a creature), and 303.4d independently states an Aura can't enchant itself; 704.5m states an Aura not attached to anything is put into its owner's graveyard.

122.1a states +1/+1 counters on a creature card in a zone other than the battlefield still add to its power; 608.2h states information is determined once when the effect is applied using the object's current info in the public zone it's in, and 611.2d states a variable in a continuous effect is determined only once.

701.40a states manifesting turns the card face down and puts that card onto the battlefield from wherever it is; here that zone is exile, not the graveyard or library that Grafdigger's Cage restricts.
406.7 states an object in exile that becomes exiled doesn't change zones but becomes a new object that has just been exiled, and 406.3 states exiled cards are face up by default.

614.4 states a replacement effect must exist before the event it replaces, so Skullbriar needed its counter-retention ability before leaving the graveyard; 406.7 states re-exiling doesn't change zones (and 122.2 states counters are only lost on a zone change), and 406.3 states exiled cards are face up by default.

702.2b states any creature dealt damage by a deathtouch source is destroyed as a state-based action, killing the Wurms; 704.5g states lethal damage destroys a creature, which is what the Wurms' combined 15 damage does to Fathom Feeder.
601.2c states the caster announces an appropriate object for each target the spell requires; being a creature is the only criterion Artful Dodge imposes, and usefulness isn't part of target legality.
702.6a states equip is an activated ability of Equipment, so Null Rod's restriction on activated abilities of artifacts stops it.

608.2h states that when an effect needs information from a specific object that is no longer in the zone it was expected to be in, last known information is used; the Oran-Rief Invoker's last known info in the graveyard was ability-less thanks to Yixlid Jailer.

113.7a states an activated ability exists on the stack independently of its source and isn't affected by the source's removal; 608.2b states a spell or ability with all targets illegal on resolution is removed from the stack and does nothing.
117.3b states the active player receives priority after a spell resolves, so Addison can flash Past in Flames' effect back before Nathalie ever gets priority.
602.2b states activating an ability follows rules 601.2b-i, and 601.2h states costs are paid during that process, so the creature card was already exiled before anyone could respond.
712.14 states a double-faced card put onto the battlefield from a zone other than the stack enters with its front face up by default, so it returns as Elbrus, the Binding Blade.

603.3 states a triggered ability goes on the stack only the next time a player would receive priority, so Sorin's ability resolves fully first; 400.7 states an object that changes zones becomes a new object with no relation to its previous existence, so the dies trigger can't find Relentless Dead in the graveyard.

608.2c states instructions are followed in the order written, so the fight happens before the delayed trigger is created; 603.7a states a delayed triggered ability won't trigger until it has actually been created, even if the trigger event just occurred.

113.7a states the source can still perform the action even though it no longer exists (using last known information), and 608.2h states that if an ability says an object does something, it's the object as it most recently existed that does it.
601.2c states the player must announce an appropriate object for each target the spell requires; an Illusion token isn't appropriate for Mask of the Mimic's nontoken creature requirement.

406.6 states the exile ability and the 'exiled with this object' ability are linked, and 607.1 states a linked ability refers only to objects affected by its partner on that same object; 400.7 states the returned Specter is a new object with no relation to its previous existence.

603.7 states each resolution can create a delayed triggered ability, so two resolutions grant two instances; 602.5c states a use restriction on an acquired activated ability applies only to that ability as acquired from that object, not to other identically worded instances.
700.2 states a modal ability is a single ability with two or more options, so its once-per-turn activation restriction applies to the ability as a whole regardless of mode.

106.12 states 'tap for mana' means activating any mana ability of that permanent with {T} in its cost, and 106.12a states an ability triggering when a permanent is tapped for mana triggers whenever such a mana ability resolves and produces mana.

712.14a states that if a player is instructed to put a card that isn't a double-faced card onto the battlefield transformed, that card stays in its current zone, so Sakashima remains in the graveyard.

111.8 states a token that has left the battlefield can't come back (111.7 states it ceases to exist); 509.1h states a creature remains blocked even if all creatures blocking it are removed; 510.1c states a blocked creature with no blockers assigns no combat damage.

603.3d states putting a triggered ability on the stack follows 601.2c-d, so a legal target must be chosen then; 608.2d states other choices offered by the effect are announced only while applying it on resolution.

616.1g states that when one replacement effect applies to an event and another applies to an event contained within it, the inner effect can't be chosen until the outer one has been; entering the battlefield is contained within creating the tokens, so Parallel Lives applies before Gather Specimens.
701.17c states an effect that refers to a milled card can find that card in whatever public zone it moved to, so Predict still sees the named card even though Rest in Peace exiled it.

616.2 states a replacement effect can become applicable as the result of another replacement effect modifying the event, and 616.1f states the choose-and-apply process repeats using effects that are now applicable; Anointed Procession only becomes applicable once Crafty Cutpurse makes Nancy the creator.

616.2 states an effect can become applicable because another replacement effect modified the event, and 616.1f states the process repeats with newly applicable effects; Doubling Season only applies after Gather Specimens moves the tokens to Nicole.

616.2/616.1f state that applying Gather Specimens makes Crafty Cutpurse applicable and the process repeats; 614.5 states a replacement effect gets only one opportunity to affect an event or its modified versions, so Gather Specimens can't apply a second time.

616.1g states the effect applying to the contained event (Progenitor Mimic's enters-as-a-copy effect) can't be chosen until the effect applying to the outer creation event (Primal Vigor) has been; 616.2 states each new token's own copy effect then becomes applicable and is chosen separately.

608.2b states a spell resolves as long as not all of its targets are illegal, and illegal targets aren't affected; 701.14b states that if one of the creatures instructed to fight is an illegal target, neither fights or deals damage.

707.2 states a copy takes only copiable values and that counters and other effects aren't copied; 400.7d states an ability of a permanent can reference what mana was spent to cast the spell that became it, so the copied ability counts the {U}{R} spent on Clone.

603.3d states targets for a triggered ability are chosen as it's put on the stack, while 608.2d states other choices offered by the effect, such as 'you may have it fight', are announced on resolution.
603.10 states objects existing immediately after an event are checked against trigger conditions, and Blood Operative is already in the graveyard at that moment, so its surveil trigger triggers.
702.15e states that multiple sources with lifelink dealing damage at the same time cause separate life gain events, and its own example is Ajani's Pridemate triggering twice.
